Subject: Post-call notes & next steps (model fit / prompt collection)

Thanks again for taking the time today — really useful call. Quick recap and proposed next steps for visibility: 

- Goal: determine model fit for Acme's customer-support summarization and policy-compliance assistant. Primary constraints: 1) sub-200ms median latency target for short prompts, 2) low hallucination on policy-related Q&A, 3) PII redaction requirements.
- Action items for Acme: please upload a representative prompt set (customer queries + expected outputs) and any known edge cases or failure examples. If any prompts include PII, mark them or replace with <REDACTED>.
- Our commitments: we'll run a model-fit eval across a recommended model shortlist, return token/cost estimates, and provide a suggested rollout plan (canary -> scale).

I've attached the post-call notes and will follow up with recommended model list + benchmark links tomorrow.

Attachments: post-call-notes.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Acme Legal <contracts@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for Acme - next steps

Hi Ethan — thanks, and great to hear you'll upload the set. Below are the recommended models and the evaluation we plan to run. Also included prompt-upload guidance and redaction notes.

Recommended shortlist (initial run):
- redwood-2.1-large-instruct (best-quality baseline)
- r-instruct-1.0-quant (cost-efficient quantized variant; slightly lower quality on rare legal phrasing)
- redwood-2.1-chat-medium (lower latency, good for short-turn interactions)

What we'll benchmark for each model: quality (ROUGE / human spot-checks on policy Q&A), latency (p50/p95), cost per 1k tokens, and hallucination rate on a curated policy set.

Prompt upload guidance: preferred format is a CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output (optional), tags (security/personal/edge_case), redaction_flag (yes/no). If easier, a single newline-delimited text file is fine — include an index header. See attached prompt-upload-instructions.md.

Redaction guidance (short):
- Replace email addresses, phone numbers, account IDs with <REDACTED_EMAIL>, <REDACTED_PHONE>, <REDACTED_ID>.
- For legal case excerpts, replace names/entities with placeholders and annotate in tags.
- If you cannot redact, mark redaction_flag=yes and we can run the eval in a Private deployment or with our dedicated review workflow.

Edge cases to highlight: threads with mixed instruction + policy, multi-turn context with long KV caches, and examples where the model must defer/route to a human. The more negative examples (where current assistants fail), the better for regression testing.

Attachments: recommended_models.pdf, prompt-upload-instructions.md

I'll kick off the initial eval once we have the file. If you prefer, we can schedule a short handoff with engineering to walk through the CSV schema.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for Acme - internal notes

Looping in a couple quick internal notes for the eval plan and potential quality-regression risks: 

- Please ask Acme to include at least 20 negative examples where the current assistant hallucinated or provided overly permissive policy answers; these are the most informative for our regressions.
- For metrics: include an explicit human-judged label column (PASS/FAIL) for policy Q&A samples where possible — makes our thresholding simpler.
- Redaction/workflow: if Acme marks redaction_flag=yes, we'll propose running that subset in a Private deployment (customer-managed network + KMS) to avoid handling raw PII in the hosted pipeline.
- Prompt variants: request short-form and long-form variants for the same prompt_id to evaluate KV cache effects (e.g., prefix length variations).

Also, Laura — can you prep the lightweight eval harness (script + scoring rubric) we used for the Beta; we can reuse that to produce ROUGE and hallucination-rate numbers and human spot checks. I can take lead on model selection comparisons and cost math.

Thanks,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
